title: Phase Diagram Triple Point Interactive Explorer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive 3D phase diagram explorer centered on the triple point of water. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Use an OrbitControls-enabled perspective camera starting at position (0, 5, 12) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Background color: #0a0a1a (dark navy).

## Phase Diagram Surface
- Render a 3D phase diagram as a mesh surface in the XZ plane (X = temperature in Kelvin, Z = pressure in Pascals, Y = visual height for aesthetics).
- Temperature axis: 200K to 700K. Pressure axis: 10 Pa to 1e7 Pa (log scale for Z mapping).
- The diagram must show three distinct colored regions: solid (ice blue, #88ccff), liquid (blue, #2266ff), gas/vapor (red-orange, #ff6644).
- Phase boundary curves must be rendered as bright LineSegments (white or yellow) separating the three regions.
- The triple point of water is at T=273.16K, P=611.657 Pa. Mark it with a glowing sphere (emissive green, radius 0.3).
- The critical point is at T=647.096K, P=22.064 MPa. Mark it with a glowing sphere (emissive magenta, radius 0.25).

## Interactive Probe Marker
- Render a bright yellow cone (pointing down, height 0.5, radius 0.2) as the 'probe marker' that the user moves across the diagram.
- The probe starts at T=350K, P=101325 Pa (standard atmospheric, liquid region).
- Arrow keys move the probe: Left/Right change temperature by ±10K per press, Up/Down change pressure by a multiplicative factor of 2 (Up doubles, Down halves).
- Clamp temperature to [200, 700] and pressure to [10, 1e7].
- The probe marker position on the 3D surface must update in real time.

## Phase Detection Logic
- Implement simplified phase boundary detection:
  - Solid-Liquid boundary: P > 611.657 and T < 273.16
  - Liquid-Gas boundary (Clausius-Clapeyron approximation): P_boundary(T) = 611.657 * exp((2.5e6 / 461.5) * (1/273.16 - 1/T)) for T in [273.16, 647.096]
  - Solid-Gas (sublimation): P_boundary(T) = 611.657 * exp((2.83e6 / 461.5) * (1/273.16 - 1/T)) for T < 273.16
  - At T >= 647.096 and P >= 22.064e6: supercritical fluid
- Determine the current phase at the probe position: 'solid', 'liquid', 'gas', or 'supercritical'.

## Molecule Visualization Chamber
- In the top-right area of the 3D scene (offset at x=8, y=0, z=0), render a transparent glass box (3x3x3) that shows a particle simulation of the current phase.
- Populate with 30 small spheres representing molecules.
- Solid phase: molecules vibrate in a tight grid pattern (amplitude < 0.1), colored ice-blue.
- Liquid phase: molecules move randomly within the box with moderate speed (0.02 per frame), colored blue.
- Gas phase: molecules move fast (0.06 per frame) and bounce off walls, colored orange.
- Supercritical: molecules move at 0.04 speed, colored magenta, with slight clustering behavior.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Overlay a semi-transparent panel (top-left, 320px wide) showing:
  - Current Temperature (K) with id='hud-temp'
  - Current Pressure (Pa) with id='hud-pressure'
  - Current Phase with id='hud-phase'
  - Distance to Triple Point (Euclidean in normalized coords) with id='hud-triple-dist'
- Add three DOM buttons:
  - 'Snap to Triple Point' (id='btn-triple'): instantly moves probe to T=273.16K, P=611.657 Pa.
  - 'Snap to Critical Point' (id='btn-critical'): moves probe to T=647.096K, P=22.064e6 Pa.
  - 'Reset' (id='btn-reset'): returns probe to initial T=350K, P=101325 Pa.
- Add a checkbox (id='chk-boundaries') labeled 'Show Boundaries' (default checked). Toggling it shows/hides the phase boundary lines.

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain a history stack of probe positions (temperature, pressure).
- Pressing 'U' undoes the last probe move (restores previous T, P).
- Pressing 'R' redoes a previously undone move.
- History stack max depth: 50.

## State Management (CRITICAL)
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - temperature: number (current probe temperature in K)
  - pressure: number (current probe pressure in Pa)
  - phase: string ('solid' | 'liquid' | 'gas' | 'supercritical')
  - probePosition: {x: number, y: number, z: number} (3D world position of probe marker)
  - triplePointDistance: number (Euclidean distance in normalized T/P space from probe to triple point)
  - criticalPointDistance: number (distance to critical point)
  - moleculeCount: number (should be 30)
  - moleculeAvgSpeed: number (average speed of molecules in chamber)
  - boundariesVisible: boolean
  - historyLength: number (current undo stack length)
  - redoLength: number (current redo stack length)
  - phaseChanges: number (counter incremented each time the phase changes)
  - animationRunning: boolean (true while animation loop is active)
  - frameCount: number (incremented each frame)

## Animation
- Use requestAnimationFrame loop. Update molecule positions, probe marker, and HUD every frame. Increment frameCount each frame.
physics_constraints: Clausius-Clapeyron equation governs liquid-gas boundary: P = 611.657 * exp((2.5e6/461.5)*(1/273.16 - 1/T)). Sublimation curve: P = 611.657 * exp((2.83e6/461.5)*(1/273.16 - 1/T)). Triple point exactly at T=273.16K, P=611.657Pa. Critical point at T=647.096K, P=22.064e6Pa. Molecule speeds must reflect phase: solid<0.1 amplitude, liquid~0.02, gas~0.06, supercritical~0.04. Temperature clamped [200,700]K, pressure clamped [10,1e7]Pa. Undo/redo must preserve exact T,P values with zero drift.
